explanation: Same four verses (Vāgīśa and others bow to Gajānana; Maheśvara whose breath the Vedas are; the king commanded Mādhava to expound the Veda; Mādhava, having condensed the two Mīmāṃsās, sets out to tell the Veda's meaning). Vol 1 prints 'yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syus taṃ namāmi' (supports the NOTE's 'may be / I bow') and 'tādṛśaṃ dadhre bukka-mahīpatiḥ' (names King Bukka; new English has only 'the king', letters damaged). Vol 1 also has vv.4-5 (Mādhava recommends his younger brother Sāyaṇa; Bukka orders Sāyaṇa) which the new text lacks; Vol 1 itself notes they are absent from the Telugu copies.
Both: Yajurveda explained first because of the Adhvaryu's pre-eminence, the Ṛgveda now 'for the Hotṛ'; the first chapter to be learned by tradition, after which the intelligent man can grasp all.

vol1_location: l.5743-5813 and 5843-5849, Ch.2 (pp.350-353): Puruṣa-sūkta, 'sahasraśīrṣā', Indra-Mitra-Varuṇa, Vājasaneyins
explanation: Same objection (Ṛgveda is named first everywhere, so its exposition should come first); same quotation 'tasmād yajñāt sarvahuta ṛcaḥ sāmāni…' (RV 10.90.9); yajña = the Supreme Lord, sarvahuta = invoked by all, no contradiction with Indra etc. since He abides in their forms; same 'indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇam agnim', 'ekaṃ sad viprā bahudhā vadanty agniṃ yamaṃ mātariśvānam', and the Vājasaneyin 'eṣa u hy eva sarve devāḥ' (Br.Up. 1.4.6). Only a citation number differs: new 'ṛ. 1.164.46'; Vol 1 prints '1-164-86' in the Sanskrit block but 'I.164.46' in its English footnote.

Both: the ṛc is pre-eminent also as the cause of firmness of the sacrifice's parts; Taittirīyas (TS 6.5.10.3): what is done with sāman or yajus is loose, what with ṛc is firm. Vol 1's Sanskrit supports the NOTE's guess ('yajñāṅga-dārḍhya-hetutvāt').

Same argument (Brāhmaṇas cite a ṛc; Yajurveda mantra sections have many ṛcs; sāmans rest on ṛcs; Atharvans mostly read ṛcs; Chāndogya, Muṇḍaka, Tāpanīya order). Vol 1 reads 'ādṛtatvād abhyarhitatvam' and 'sāmnāṃ… ṛgāśritatvam', which supports the NOTEs' guesses. Quotations differ in their endings: new 'sāmavedam ātharvaṇaṃ ceti' (Chāndogya) and 'atharvaṇa iti' (Muṇḍaka), Vol 1 'ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham iti' and 'atharvaveda iti'; the new English follows the supplied letters; sense unchanged.

Both: granted the Ṛgveda comes first in study, brahmayajña and japa; but since knowledge of meaning serves performance of sacrifice and there the Yajurveda is principal, its exposition first is proper; supported by RV 10.71.11 ('ṛcāṃ tvaḥ poṣam āste…').

Same Nirukta 1.8 explanation of the first two quarters: tva = one, the Hotṛ gathers scattered ṛcs and fixes 'this much is this śastra' (this is the 'nourishment'); the udgātṛ sings the gāyatra among the śakvarīs, from √śak, 'by these he could kill Vṛtra' (Kauṣītaki Br. 23.2). Vol 1's Kannada gloss adds that 'Indra' was empowered; the Sanskrit does not name him.

Same Brahmā explanation and same Chāndogya 4.16 (mind and speech paths; Brahmā alone prepares the mind-path). Vol 1's printed Sanskrit and gloss read 'prāyaścitta-karman' (permission for an expiatory rite) where the supplied Sanskrit reads 'praṇayanādi-karman' ('Brahman, shall I carry forward the waters?', 'Om, carry forward'). Vol 1's own embedded English footnote and the Kannada text say fetching water, which agrees with the new English; the new English follows the supplied Sanskrit.

Both: the Adhvaryu 'measures out the measure of the sacrifice'; adhvaryu restored to adhvarayu, 'yokes the sacrifice' (parts) / 'leader of the sacrifice' (purport); Nirukta 7.12 (mantrā mananāt…); the sacrifice's body is formed in the Yajurveda, stotra and śastra supplied by the other two, sāmans depend on ṛcs, so Ṛgveda next. The NOTE on the RV 10.71.11 reference is not answerable from Vol 1 (its Sanskrit there is garbled).

Same objection (no Veda, hence no Ṛgveda; no definition or proof; logicians' view); same failed definitions: 'last of perception, inference, scripture' over-extends to Manu's smṛtis; 'not of human origin' fails since the Lord made it; 'not made by an embodied being' fails because of 'sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ'.

Same: Vedas were produced by particular beings Agni, Vāyu, Āditya ('ṛgveda evāgner ajāyata, yajurvedo vāyoḥ, sāmaveda ādityāt'), the Lord being maker as impeller. Citation differs: new 'Aitareya Br. 5.5.7', Vol 1 'Ai. Brā. 5-32'. Vol 1's Sanskrit 'jīvaviśeṣair agnivāyvādityair vedānām utpāditatvāt' supports the NOTE's guess.
Both: 'mass of words consisting of mantra and brāhmaṇa' fails because it is not determined which is which.

Same: the Chāndogya sentence 'Ṛgvedaṃ bhagavo'dhyemi … ātharvaṇaṃ caturtham' is itself in the Veda, so self-dependence ('no one can climb on his own shoulder'); smṛti 'veda eva dvijātīnāṃ niḥśreyasakaraḥ paraḥ' is rooted in the same text; perception etc. unfit; popular acceptance like 'the sky is blue'; the prior view ends. Vol 1's Sanskrit also has Yājñavalkya-smṛti only in its gloss, the new text gives 1.40.

Same reply: mantra-brāhmaṇa-ness is a faultless definition (Āpastamba Yajña-paribhāṣā 31); nature of both and 'not of human origin' to be explained later; proofs scripture, smṛti, popular acceptance; as pots lack self-luminosity but sun and moon shine, so the Veda of unblunted power presents itself; the 'injunction can make known past, present, future…' quotation is in Vol 1 only in English; the Veda cannot be refuted by any sceptic (Cārvāka in the Sanskrit).

Same: grant a Veda, still not worth a commentary since not a pramāṇa; the two definitions (instrument of right experience / reaching a not-yet-reached object); some mantras convey no meaning: 'amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭiḥ' (RV 1.169.3), 'yādṛśmin dhāyi…' (5.44.8), 'sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītū' (10.106.6), 'pāntamanyus…' (10.89.5). Vol 1's wording 'being a means of knowledge is far removed' supports 'instrumentality' as the NOTE guessed.

Same: 'adhaḥ svid āsīd upari svid āsīt' (RV 10.129.5) gives a doubtful sense, like 'post or man'; 'oṣadhe trāyasvainam' (darbha), 'svadhite' (razor), 'śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ' (stones) address insentient things as sentient, like 'two moons'; 'eka eva rudro' and 'sahasrāṇi sahasraśo ye rudrāḥ' contradict, like 'I am silent all my life'. Vol 1 gives TS 4.5.11.1 at p.371 and 4.5.11.5 at p.381; the new English has .5.
Same: 'āpa undantu' for moistening the sacrificer's head at shaving; 'śubhike śira āroha…' for a flower-made śubhikā on the heads of bridegroom and bride. Unit ends mid-sentence, as the page does.

vol1_location: first sentences l.6425-6432 (p.371); the reply is not in Vol 1 (printed pp.372-373 are absent: Vol 1 passes from p.371 to p.374)
explanation: New (Sanskrit supplied: 'tasmān mantrabhāgo na pramāṇam'): 'Therefore the mantra portion is not a means of knowledge', because both mantras restate what is popularly known. Vol 1 (Sanskrit l.6428): 'tasmāt smṛtibhāgo na pramāṇam', 'the smṛti portion'. The literal clash is probably a slip in Vol 1's transcription: its own gloss (l.6432) says 'this portion of the Veda' and the next page (l.6458) says 'mantra-portion is authoritative'. So the new English follows the Sanskrit and the context better. The second half of the unit (Yāska explained 'amyak…' in the Nirukta; the blind man and the post: 'it is not the post's fault') has no counterpart at this place in Vol 1; the same proverb is used much later, l.7936-7960.

vol1_location: not in Vol 1; searched pp.371-374 (l.6414-6460) and grepped Part II for 'profund', 'adhaḥ svid' purpose, 'kō addhā', 'Ko addha'
explanation: New: 'adhaḥ svid' is not for producing doubt but to show the profundity of the supreme reality; confirmed by 'ko addhā veda' (RV 3.54.5). Vol 1's printed pp.372-373 are missing; no matching text elsewhere.

vol1_location: closing sentence l.6453-6458 (p.374); related ideas at l.6641-6652 (p.381) and 6680-6695 (p.382)
explanation: Placed: the last sentence (water on the head is popular, the favour of the presiding deities is not, so the mantra reveals the unknown; therefore the mantra portion is a pramāṇa). Vol 1 p.381 also has the answer by presiding deities of herbs (Vyāsa's 'abhimānivyapadeśa'), and the one Rudra with many forms is in Vol 1 only as an objector's defence (l.6680-6695). The first two-thirds of this unit sat on missing pp.372-373 and cannot be compared directly.

Same: Jaimini in the Mantra-adhikaraṇa (1.2.31-53) lays down that mantras have an intended meaning; prior view in the sūtra 'tad-artha-śāstrāt' (1.2.31): the Brāhmaṇa 'puroḍāśaṃ prathayati' already says what 'uru prathasva' says (TS 1.1.8, TB 3.2.8.4), so the mantras serve by utterance alone.

Same: if for utterance an unseen purpose is imagined, if for meaning a seen one; sūtra 'vākya-niyamāt' (1.2.32): 'agnir mūrdhā divaḥ kakut' (RV 8.44.16) has a fixed order though a reversed order conveys the same meaning; objection that the order rule serves the unseen while recitation still conveys meaning.

Same: sūtra 'buddha-śāstrāt' (1.2.33): 'agnīd agnīn vihara' (TS 6.3.1.2), the Āgnīdhra knows it from study, 'no one puts a sandal on a foot already sandalled'; reminding objection; sūtra 'avidyamāna-vacanāt' (1.2.34): 'catvāri śṛṅgā…' (RV 4.58.3) names no real implement; sūtra 'acetane'rtha-bandhanāt' (1.2.35): 'oṣadhe trāyasva', 'śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ'.

Same: 'abhimāni-vyapadeśa' (Ve.Sū. 2.1.5) objection; sūtra 'artha-vipratiṣedhāt' (1.2.36): 'aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣam' (RV 1.89.10) and 'eka eva rudro' / 'sahasrāṇi sahasraśo ye rudrāḥ'; defence 'you alone are mother and father', one Rudra taking many forms. (Vol 1 prints the Vedānta-sūtra as 2-1-5 at l.6641 and 2-1-3 in its gloss; the new English has 2.1.5.)

Same: sūtra 'svādhyāyavad-vacanāt' (1.2.37): the woman Pūrṇikā pounds, a boy near her learns his pestle mantra without intent to convey meaning, so too the mantra at the rite; objection that the Adhvaryu does intend meaning and can be understood; next sūtra 'avijñeyāt' (1.2.38).

Same: 'amyak sā ta indra ṛṣṭiḥ' and 'sṛṇyeva jarbharī turpharītū' cannot be understood; objection that Nigama, Nirukta and grammar exist; sūtra 'anitya-saṃyogān mantrānarthakyam' (1.2.39): 'kiṃ te kṛṇvanti kīkaṭeṣu' (RV 3.53.14), Kīkaṭa a country, Naicāśākha a city, Pramaganda a king, so the mantra did not exist before him; the prior view ends.

Same: sūtra 'avaśiṣṭas tu vākyārthaḥ' (1.2.40; Vol 1 heading 'api śiṣṭasya'); 'tu' rules out utterance alone; the sentence-meaning from action and factors is the same in the world and the Veda; mantras are uttered to illuminate meaning, a seen purpose.

Same argument: the mantra beginning 'abhrir asi nāry asi' already gives the taking of the digging stick, so the Brāhmaṇa 'caturbhir abhrim ādatte' would be pointless; sūtra 'guṇārthena punaḥ-śrutiḥ' (1.2.41): it enjoins the number four, else any one of the four mantras would do; same for 'imām agṛbhṇan raśanām' and 'aśvābhidhānīm ādatte'; sūtra 'parisaṃkhyā' (1.2.42) on 'he does not take the donkey's tether'. Citations differ: new VS 11.10 and ŚB 6.3.1.39 (abhri), VS 22.2 and ŚB 13.18.1 (raśanā); Vol 1 TS 4.1.1.3 and 5.1.1.4, TS 4.1.2.1 and 5.1.2.1. Sense unchanged.

Same: the three faults of parisaṃkhyā (the word loses its own meaning, a prohibition-meaning is imagined, the obtained donkey's rope is set aside) are denied because the donkey's rope is not obtained: the sentence 'perform the taking with this mantra' is supposed, the mark 'rope' gives a general taking, specialised by the direct 'aśvābhidhānīm'; so no setting aside of what is obtained.

Same: objection that the Brāhmaṇa 'prathayati' for 'uru prathasva' stays pointless; sūtra 'arthavādo vā' (1.2.43), the injunction is for the arthavāda 'yajñapatim eva tat prathayati'; the source of the spreading is the mantra's utterance by the Adhvaryu, 'as in the world he who says "do" causes it to be done'.
Same: sūtra 'aviruddhaṃ param' (1.2.44): the order-rule's unseen purpose is not denied, but the seen purpose of conveying meaning must not be neglected.
Same: 'prokṣaṇīr āsādaya' (VS 1.28) restates a known matter, 'one who has sandals…'; sūtra 'sampreṣa-karmaṇo garhānupalambhaḥ saṃskārāt' (1.2.45): no fault, a saṃskāra from the rule.

Same: sūtra 'abhidhāne 'rthavādaḥ' (1.2.46); 'catvāri śṛṅgā' read figuratively: four priests the horns, the three pressings the feet, wife and sacrificer the two heads, the seven metres the hands, bound threefold by the three Vedas, 'bull' because it showers desires, 'roars' with stotra and śastra, 'great god … has entered mortals' so only men are entitled; river described with cakravāka breasts, kāśa garment, śaivāla hair; 'oṣadhe trāyasva', 'śṛṇota grāvāṇaḥ' as praise; then 1.2.47 announced. One word differs: the new English translates the supplied 'hasadantāvalī' as 'a row of laughing teeth'; Vol 1 prints 'haṃsa-dantāvalī' and its English says 'white swans for her lines of teeth'; Vol 1 seems closer to the figure, the supplied letters allow either.

Same: sūtra 1.2.47, 'you alone are father, you alone are mother', one Rudra in a rite of one Rudra, a hundred in a rite of a hundred; sūtra 'vidyā-vacanam asaṃyogāt': nothing said at the boy's study because Pūrṇikā's pounding and the boy have no connection with a sacrifice. Vol 1 numbers the sūtra 1-2-48 at l.7305, which is the NOTE's guess.

Same: sūtra 'sataḥ param avijñānam' (1.2.49): an existing meaning is unknown through negligence and laziness; by Nigama, Nirukta and grammar the meaning is inferred from the root; 'jarbharī turpharītū' are names of the Aśvins (duals; hymn RV 10.106, 'aśvinoḥ kāmam aprāḥ' v.11); Nirukta 'bhartārau', 'hantārau'; so 'amyak sā ta' too.

Same: the objection from impermanent connection (Pramaganda, RV 3.53.14) answered by sūtra 'uktas tu anitya-saṃyogaḥ' (1.2.50). Vol 1's Sanskrit reads 'anitya-saṃyogān', confirming the sense 'impermanent' that the NOTE's correction supplies.

Same: the first-pāda answer: in the prior view 'Kāṭhaka, Kālāpaka' (person-names) and 'anitya-darśanāt' ('babaraḥ prāvāhaṇir akāmayata', TS 7.1.10.2), answered by 'paraṃ tu śruti-sāmānya-mātram' (1.1.31): Babara is an imitation of a sound, the wind, Prāvāhaṇi 'flowing forth with force'. Sūtra number for 'anitya-darśanāt' differs: new 1.1.25; Vol 1 'Jaimini Sutra 1-1-28' (its Sanskrit text reads 'nitya-darśanāc ca' while its gloss and English read 'anitya', which agrees with the new English).

Same: objection that 'seen purpose' is only reasoning, no Vedic mark; sūtra 'liṅgopadeśaś ca tad-arthavat' (1.2.51): 'āgneyy āgnīdhram upatiṣṭheta', the Brāhmaṇa does not cite 'agne naya' (RV 1.189.1) but describes the verse by its deity with a taddhita suffix, so the sentence-meaning is relied on.

Same: sūtra 'ūhaḥ' (1.2.52): the model mantra 'anv enaṃ mātā manyatām anu pitānu bhrātā' (MS 4.13.4), dual 'enau', plural 'enān'; the Brāhmaṇa 'na mātā vardhate na pitā': bodily growth cannot be denied, so growth in words (mātarau etc.) is meant, hence the other word 'enam' adapts to the meaning. Vol 1's 'vardhate' supports the NOTE's 'grows'.

Same: sūtra 'vidhi-śabdāc ca' (1.2.53), the Brāhmaṇa word explaining a mantra: 'śataṃ himāḥ śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvyāsam ity evaitad āha' (ŚB 2.3.4.21); if the mantra had no intended meaning, nothing would be explained.

Same two summary verses: are 'uru prathasva' and similar mantras only a cause of the unseen, or do they illuminate the spreading of the puroḍāśa; no, since a seen purpose is better than an unseen. Reference differs: new 'Jaimini-nyāya (mālā) 1.3.4', Vol 1 '1-2-4'; the supplied word is 'bhānāt' (illumination), Vol 1 prints 'dhyānāt' but glosses it 'declaratory power', which agrees with the new English.

Same: grant the mantra portion, but the Brāhmaṇa portion (vidhi and arthavāda; Āpastamba) fails: injunctions set going the unset-going (karma-kāṇḍa, 'āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ puroḍāśaṃ nirvapanti dīkṣaṇīyāyām') and make known the unknown (brahma-kāṇḍa, 'ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt'); the 'jartila-yavāgū' injunction is unauthoritative since 'anāhutir vai jartilāś ca gavīdhukāś ca'. Only the Āraṇyaka citation differs: new 'e. u. 1.1', Vol 1 'Ai. Ā. 2-4-1'.

Same: many injunctions forbidden in the Aitareya and Taittirīya Brāhmaṇas; the Aitareya censures the pre-sunrise homa ('tasmād udite hotavyam'); Taittirīyas 'yad anudite sūrye…' and then censure the post-sunrise one ('yathātithaye pradrutāya śūnyāyāvasathāyāhāryaṃ haranti'); 'atirātre ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhṇāti' against 'nātirātre…'; Jyotiṣṭoma fruit not seen after the rite, unlike satisfaction after food. Differences: the supplied 'tat tan nāvṛtyam' (new: 'not to be repeated') against Vol 1 'tat tan nādṛtyam' ('not to be regarded'); the first Taittirīya quotation is given as 'Ai. Br. 5.5.4' in the new text (the NOTE asks) and as 'Tai. Brā. 2-1-2-7' in Vol 1, which settles the NOTE; the supplied 'dīpa' against Vol 1 'doṣa' (fault), which also confirms the NOTE; the second quotation 'Tai. Brā. 2.1.27' against 2-1-2-12. Vol 1 adds a Prajāpati-Agni-Sūrya story and an Atirātra stotra table that the new text lacks. The unit breaks off at 'mutually-' (Vol 1 continues with the Aitareya 'ātmā vā idam' against Taittirīya 'asad vā idam', l.7736-7753).
